sections.heading: C2 — Cell phones, drowsy driving and the safety campaign page, with behavior confusables
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Cell phones, drowsy driving and the safety campaign page, with behavior confusables

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A35
Using a hand-held cell phone while driving, texting included, is illegal, so you may not drive while holding your phone. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A35
Adult drivers may make calls hands-free, but should keep phone use to a minimum. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A35
Safer phone habits are to call only in emergencies, let a passenger place the call when possible, or pull safely off the road and stop first. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A35
Let voicemail pick up incoming calls and keep any conversation short. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A35
Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone at all while driving, even hands-free, except to call 911 in an emergency. [A35]
Why it matters: the hands-free allowance does not apply to drivers under 18.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A35
Lack of sleep slows reaction time, lowers awareness and impairs judgment much as drugs or alcohol do, sharply raising crash risk. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A35
People who drive many miles daily, people with sleep disorders and people on certain medicines face a higher risk of drowsiness. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A35
Drowsiness warning signs include eyes closing or blurring, trouble holding your head up, nonstop yawning and drifting, disconnected thoughts. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A35
Other drowsiness signs are not recalling the last few miles, missing your exit, repeatedly leaving your lane and repeatedly changing speed. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A35
If you get tired or sleepy at the wheel, the best response is to rest or switch drivers. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A36
The manual's campaign page states that one-third of fatal crashes are caused by distracted driving, with cell phone use among the leading distractions. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A36
Every year tens of thousands of people are arrested on Maryland roads for drunk or drugged driving. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A36
Before going out, plan a safe way home and name a sober driver, since an impaired-driving arrest brings large fines, possible jail and thousands of dollars in court costs. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A33
The legal under-the-influence line is a BAC of .08, but impairment and criminal charges are possible at lower levels, and drivers under 21 may not drink any alcohol. [A33]
Why it matters: group_hint alcohol-limits; prereq_hint sec08-F02; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec08-F03, sec08-F04, sec08-F08.
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A35
Drivers 18 and older may use a phone hands-free, while drivers under 18 may not use one at all except for a 911 call, and no driver may use a hand-held phone. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint cell-phones; prereq_hint sec08-F27; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec08-F27, sec08-F28, sec08-F31.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A33
The open-container ban is tied to the passenger area, and that area is defined as the seats plus anywhere occupants can easily reach while sitting, not just the seats themselves. [A33]
Why it matters: group_hint open-container; prereq_hint sec08-F10; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec08-F11, sec08-F12.
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A35
Drowsiness impairs judgment and reaction time much like alcohol, and the cure is rest or a new driver rather than pushing on. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint impairment; prereq_hint sec08-F32; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F32, sec08-F36.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0035]
